propositions: Plan-review and completion-verifier gates cannot audit measurement context (environment, principal, privilege posture, instrument type) because evidence is attested before measurement occurs and verifier trust is by design; escapes occur when measurements are taken under conditions (broader privilege, simulation vs live call, wrong account) that structurally prevent them from observing the failure they claim to rule out.

Four independent escapes in epic 061c share a root cause: measurements lacking recorded provenance (Bedrock cached under wrong AWS account and identity; simulator returning confident wrong conclusion for bedrock:Converse vs bedrock:InvokeModel; tests with unexercised discriminating conjuncts; grep-verified claims missing dependencies) were invisible to repo-grounded review tools.

Forcing measurement provenance into the attestation record as human-readable text fields (environment, principal, privilege_posture, instrument) enables existing repo-checkable machinery to detect contradictions (e.g. plan attests account X while IaC names account Y) deterministically without making gates observe the world.

An additional escape class occurs when plans assert unchanged behaviour across configuration/route/provider swaps without citing the resolution path that would make the assertion verifiable, enabling defects to survive review as examples of commendable scope discipline.

The completion-verifier must not be made to re-run world measurements as validation, because its own credentials carry the same privilege-masking problem and such re-runs are expensive, flaky, and recursive.
